My counts are approximate because I tallied the rows by hand. About 100 applications are from Hispanic or Latino female applicants, and 8 were denied, a denial rate of roughly 8%. That is in line with the dataset's overall denial rate of roughly 7-9%. White, Asian, and Black female applicants and Hispanic male applicants show similar or comparable rates. Most of the 8 denials match standard risk factors. Five had debt-to-income ratios of 50% or higher, and one more reported $0 income. Only two denials (DTI 43-46%, LTV 80-85%) lack an obvious risk factor, and similar unexplained denials also appear for White, Asian, and Hispanic male applicants. Many Hispanic or Latino women were approved even with high-risk profiles, such as loan-to-value ratios of 95-97% and DTI ratios of 44-49%. The data does not show a pattern of disproportionate denial for this group. Confidence is moderate because the dataset lacks key factors such as credit score and employment history, and because a correlational summary cannot fully prove or rule out discrimination.
